# Acrolls

> Acrolls is a SvelteKit publishing and documentation framework. It turns Markdown into
> publication pages and nested documentation while the host keeps ownership of its content,
> routes, authentication, adapter, and deployment.

## Installation contract

Install one public npm package from the SvelteKit host root:

```bash
pnpm add acrolls@latest
pnpm exec acrolls --version
pnpm exec acrolls onboard --docs-dir docs --base-href /docs
```

Do not clone Acrolls into the host. Do not add `file:` links or direct `@acrolls/*`
dependencies. All consumer imports use `acrolls/*`.

## Activation sequence

1. Start in an existing SvelteKit 2.62+ or SvelteKit 3 application.
2. Install `acrolls@latest` and run `pnpm exec acrolls onboard` from the host root.
3. Write Markdown in the directory passed with `--docs-dir` (`docs` by default).
4. Configure Acrolls in the `sveltekit({ ... })` options in `vite.config.ts`. Do not create
   `svelte.config.js` for SvelteKit 3.
5. Add the generated source and routes shown by onboarding. With the defaults, documents are
   published at `/docs` and nested files map to nested URLs below `/docs`.
6. Run `pnpm exec acrolls validate ./docs`, then the host's `pnpm check` and `pnpm build`.
7. Test the docs root, a nested URL, direct refresh, an unknown slug, code highlighting,
   tables, Mermaid, navigation, and the production deployment.

## Public entrypoints

- `acrolls/mdsvex`: Markdown/mdsvex preprocessing, GFM, headings, Shiki, Mermaid, and source safety.
- `acrolls/svelte`: `Publication` and article components.
- `acrolls/docs`: `DocsShell`, navigation, breadcrumbs, TOC, and pager components.
- `acrolls/content`: content collections — `content`, `markdownGlob`, `customSource`. This is
  the recommended front door for a generated docs corpus.
- `acrolls/docs/content`: `defineDocsConfig`, docs config types, and the lower-level
  `createDocsContentSource` engine.
- `acrolls/sveltekit`: SvelteKit preprocessor and generated-source helpers.
- `acrolls/styles/foundation.css`: minimal article styles.
- `acrolls/styles/default.css`: opinionated article styles.
- `acrolls/docs/styles.css`: documentation shell styles.
- `acrolls/styles/{foundation,default,docs,tokens}.sass`: Sass entrypoints; plain Sass module
  specifiers without the extension are also supported from global Sass source files.

## CLI behavior

- `acrolls create <dir> [--base-href <path>] [--mode foundation|default] [--force|--dry-run]` scaffolds
  a new pre-wired SvelteKit docs project; it refuses a non-empty target directory unless `--force` is passed.
- `acrolls onboard [--check|--json|--non-interactive]` is the recommended read-only activation guide.
- `acrolls validate <file|directory>` checks Markdown/SVX; only `--report` writes a report.
- `acrolls init` creates a content directory unless `--dry-run` is used.
- `acrolls integrate` is conservative: dry-run reports a plan; `--yes` refuses non-SvelteKit
  hosts and existing Vite configs.
- `acrolls studio <file>` serves a loopback-only preview and may save the selected source file.
- `acrolls search-index [--site <dir>]` builds the Pagefind search bundle from the built site output.
- `acrolls api-ref <spec|dir> [--out <dir>]` generates Markdown API-reference pages from an OpenAPI,
  AsyncAPI, or GraphQL spec; JSON needs no dependency, YAML and SDL use optional `yaml`/`graphql` peers.
- `--cwd <host>` may appear before a command to target another project directory.

## Content and route defaults

- Authors write documents in `<host>/docs` unless `--docs-dir` changes it.
- The generated source is one `content({ loader: markdownGlob({ body, modules, root }), config })`
  declaration ending in `.sourceSync()`. `body` and `modules` are two `import.meta.glob` calls
  over the identical pattern: `body` lazy with `{ import: 'default' }`, `modules` eager with
  `{ eager: true }`. `root` is the stripped directory prefix.
- `content()` also takes optional `schema` (any Standard Schema validator, supplied by the host;
  failures become `ACROLLS_SCHEMA_INVALID` diagnostics that follow the existing authored/migration
  mode policy) and `filter` (receives `{ key, data, meta }`; removes a document from every
  addressable surface including direct URL access — unlike frontmatter `hidden`, which leaves
  the page unlisted but still routeable and still prerendered).
- `filter` is a publication boundary, not a confidentiality boundary. The glob loader
  materializes every file matching the glob into the module graph before `filter` runs, so a
  filtered document's compiled body can still be present in build output even though nothing
  routes to it. Secret or embargoed content belongs outside the globbed directory or behind
  host-owned authentication. A `customSource` that never returns the document does not
  materialize it at all.
- `customSource({ list })` swaps the glob loader for a CMS/API source. It is async-only, so the
  host must `await collection.source()` rather than call `sourceSync()`; the loader's `live()`
  hook is a reserved type-level seam with no implementation.
- `createAcrollsDocsSource` from `acrolls/sveltekit` still works, unchanged and warning-free.
  It is deprecated in TSDoc only and is not scheduled for removal.
- The host adds `src/routes/docs/+layout.svelte`, `src/routes/docs/+page.*`, and
  `src/routes/docs/[...slug]/+page.*` for the default `/docs` URL.
- `docs/index.md` maps to `/docs`; `docs/guides/install.md` maps to `/docs/guides/install`.
- `.md` is prose and receives source-safety normalization. `.svx` may contain intentional Svelte
  and remains fail-fast.

## Failure boundaries

- Onboarding fails when run outside a package/SvelteKit host or when flags are invalid.
- Integration refuses to overwrite an existing `vite.config.*` because plugin arrays and host
  options need review.
- Validation fails on unreadable paths, unsupported files, malformed frontmatter/Markdown/Svelte,
  duplicate routes, or strict source-safety findings.
- A build can still fail on host route/type errors, adapter configuration, missing environment
  variables, or invalid executable `.svx`.
- Acrolls does not choose an adapter, configure authentication, supply deployment credentials,
  or prove that the deployed public URL works.
